name: Semiotic

hlido_opinion.headline: A deep, mature React data-visualization library with an unusually broad chart catalog and a real accessibility discipline — a developer library, not an agent, and reviewed here through its documentation.
hlido_opinion.body: Semiotic (from the nteract org) is a React data-visualization library, and the documentation surface makes its defining trait clear immediately: breadth. The catalog spans standard XY and categorical charts (line, area, scatter, bar, box, violin), network diagrams (force-directed, chord, Sankey, tree, treemap, circle-pack), geospatial maps (choropleth, flow, cartogram), a whole 'physics' family (Galton board, collision swarm, chain reaction), and streaming/realtime frames — far more chart types than a typical charting library exposes. It is clearly a serious, mature project: there is a v3 with a migration guide, a large worked-example gallery, custom-chart tooling (glyph marks, recipe decoration), a mobile-visualization track, and — notably — a dedicated accessibility section with a Chartability audit, chart descriptions and structured navigation, which is a discipline most viz libraries treat as an afterthought. The honest framing for Hlido's readers is that this is a developer library, not an AI agent: you consume it as npm/React code, there is no API, CLI, MCP server or agent-drivable surface, and 'quality' here means the fit and correctness of the components in your own build rather than a behaviour we can exercise. On its own terms it is strong and thoughtfully built; the uncertainty is around current maintenance momentum and adoption, which the documentation surface alone doesn't establish. For React teams that need an expressive, accessibility-conscious viz layer beyond the common libraries, Semiotic is well worth evaluating from its docs and source.

tier_rationale: STEADY (75) because Semiotic is a mature, expressive React data-viz library with an unusually broad chart catalog, a v3 with migration guidance, extensive examples, custom-chart tooling and a genuine accessibility discipline (Chartability audit, chart descriptions, structured navigation). Held in the mid-70s because it is a developer library rather than an agent — no API/CLI/MCP or agent-drivable surface — and current maintenance momentum and adoption are not established by the documentation surface reviewed. It rises with visible recent-release cadence and adoption signals.
what_it_does_well: Unusually broad chart catalog — XY, categorical, network, geospatial, a physics family, and realtime/streaming frames
Mature and versioned: a v3 with a migration guide, plus a large worked-example gallery
A real accessibility discipline — Chartability audit, chart descriptions and structured navigation, rarely a first-class concern in viz libraries
Custom-chart tooling (glyph marks, recipe decoration, custom layouts) for going beyond the presets
Dedicated mobile-visualization track and a documented streaming/push model
what_it_fails_at: It is a developer React library, not an agent — no API, CLI, MCP server or agent-drivable interface
Current maintenance momentum and adoption are not evidenced on the documentation surface
Value is confined to the React ecosystem; teams on other stacks get nothing
'Quality' is the fit of components in your own build — nothing is behaviourally testable from the public surface
The sheer breadth raises a learning-curve and long-term-support question the docs alone don't answer
best_for: React and Next.js teams that need an expressive visualization layer beyond common charting libraries
Developers who need network, geospatial or physics-style visualizations, not just standard charts
Teams for whom chart accessibility (screen-reader descriptions, structured navigation) is a real requirement
not_recommended_for: Teams wanting a hosted or agent-drivable analytics/visualization service rather than a code library
Buyers who need a strong recency-of-maintenance signal before adopting a dependency
